name: Facebook
comment: FBSDKApplicationDelegate or FBSDKApplicationDelegate|FacebookCore|FBSDKCoreKit. iOS SDK for Meta's Facebook platform. Handles Facebook login, sharing and app analytics.
Detail: Owned by Meta Platforms.

name: Google Consent API
comment: Google's old SDK for collecting GDPR/CCPA ad consent. Not active anymore, was archived October 21, 2022 and replaced by Google's User messaging Platform SDK with different classes names (UMPConsentForm, UMPConsentInformation, UMPDebugSettings).
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet). Close-source and distributed via Google's mobile ads SDK

name: AdID access
comment: Native Apple class for reading a device's advertising identifier (IDFA). Built into iOS, no separate repository.
Detail: Owned by Apple Inc.

name: iOS - Device SDK
comment: Native iOS class exposing device info: model, system version, battery level, and identifierForVendor (IDFV). No separate repository.
Detail: Owned by Apple Inc. the company behind iOS and electronics such as iPhone, iPad, Mac.

name: Google AdMob
comment: SDK for Google AdMob, a mobile advertising platform: shows banner, interstitial, rewarded and native ads, and uses IDFA for ad targeting/measurement. Includes classes formerly named DFPBannerView/DFPInterstitial. Used by AdMob and AdManager, renamed GAMBannerView/GAMInterstitialAd after DoubleClick for Publishers became Google Ad Manager.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: Google Firebase
comment: SDK for Firebase, Google's app-development and analytics platform. Provides libraries, services, and tools for authentication, databases, crash reporting, and analytics.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: Google CrashLytics
comment: SDK for Crashlytics, a crash-reporting service (part of Firebase), automatically collects crash data and groups similar crashes together.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet). Formerly independent Crashlytics, acquired by Twitter (as part of Fabric); Google acquired Fabric in 2017 from Twitter.

name: Google Maps
comment: Embeds interactive Google Maps in an app: map display, markers, place search and location services.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: Google Firebase Messaging
comment: Formerly Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) renamed Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) in 2016. Cross-platform push notification service for sending notifications and data messages to apps.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: Google Sign-In
comment: Lets users authenticate into an app using their Google account.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet)

name: Google Analytics
comment: Legacy Google Analytics SDK for mobile apps (Universal Analytics). Discontinued in 2019, and replaced by Firebase Analytics and later folded into Google Analytics 4.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet)

name: Inmobi
comment: Mobile advertising network: shows banner, interstitial, native, and rewarded ads.
Detail: Owned by InMobi Pte. Ltd. Founded as mKhoj, renamed InMobi in 2008.

name: Unity3d Ads
comment: SDK for Unity3d Ads, a mobile advertising network that lets developers monetize. Supports rewarded video, interstitial and banner ads.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Unity merged with ironSource (2022), and then ad mediation from both became unified under Unity LevelPlay.

name: Moat
comment: SDK for Moat, a digital advertising analytics and measurement platform. Tracked viewability, brand safety and ad fraud metrics for advertisers and publishers. Discontinued in 2024.
Detail: Last owned by Oracle. Formerly independent Moat, acquired by Oracle in 2017.

name: Twitter MoPub
comment: SDK for MoPub. A mobile ad mediation/monetization platform for banner, interstitial, native and rewarded ads. Shut down in 2022.
Detail: Acquired by Twitter in 2013, sold to AppLovin in 2022 who merged its features into its own platform.

name: AppLovin (MAX and SparkLabs)
comment: SDK for AppLovin's MAX. Mobile ad mediation and monetization platform (MAX): displays banners, interstitial, and rewarded ads, uses mediation to see via multiple ad network which pays the most, and then shows that ad. Sparklabs is Applovin's in-house creative team which produces ad content, but it is not a separate SDK.
Detail: Owned by AppLovin Corporation. Acquired Twitter's MoPub business in 2022 and merged into MAX.

name: ChartBoost
comment: SDK for Chartboost, a mobile advertising platform for games: displays banner ads, interstitial and rewarded to help monetize in mobile games. Uses mediation to find the network that gives most revenue.
Detail: Formerly owned by Zynga who sold it to LoopMe in 2024. Currently owned by LoopMe.

name: AdColony
comment: SDK for AdColony, a mobile advertising network for video and rich media ads: shows video and interactive rich-media ads to support monetization.
Detail: Formerly owned by Digital Turbine who acquired it in 2021 from Otello Corp. Digital Turbine discontinued the SDK and sold the AdColony brand, SDK and the underlying technology to Affle (Affle MEA FZ LLC) in 2026. Currently owned by Affle.

name: Amazon Analytics (Amazon insights)
comment: SDK for Amazon Analytics, Amazon insights. Tracks app usage (sessions, purchases, custom events) for user behaviour analytics. Originally named Amazon Mobile Analytics then later merged into Amazon Pinpoint (their messaing/analytics service). Amazon Pinpoint is being closed down with customer support stopping in October 2026.
Detail: Owned by Amazon Web Services (Amazon.com Inc.).

name: Parse
comment: SDK for Parse. Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS): gives aps a ready-made backend for storing user data sending push notifications and running server-side code (cloud functions) without developers building their own server.
Detail: Acquired by Facebook (Meta) in 2013 who closed the hosted service in 2017 and open-sourced the code. Is today maintained by a volunteer open source community governed by a Project Management Committee and bears no affiliation to Meta today.

name: HockeyApp
comment: SDK for HockeyApp, a crash reporting and beta-testing tool: automatically collects a report when the app crashes, and lets developers send early/beta versions of the app to testers before public release, user behaviour analytics.
Detail: Acquired by Microsoft in 2014, then merged into Visual Studio App Center, which was retired by Microsoft end of March 2025. Service not active, HockeyApp got retired in 2019.

name: Tapjoy
comment: Mobile advertising platform known for rewarded ads: users get an in-app reward e.g game currency or extra lives if they watch an ad or complete an offer.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Formerly independent TapJoy, acquired by ironSource in 2022; merged into Unity Software Inc. in 2022.

name: Twitter Account Kit
comment: Passwordless phone-number-based login SDK (Digits), part of Twitter's Fabric Developer toolkit. Twitter discontinued Fabric/Twitter Kit and other related developer SDKs in 2018, and the service is no longer active.
Detail: Formerly Twitter is now named X Corp.

name: PlayHaven
comment: SDK for Playhaven, a mobile ad network and monetization SDK for games. Discontinued.
Detail: Merged with Kontagent in 2013/2014 to form Upsight, but Playhaven ad network was later sold out of Upsight to Science Inc. In 2014 and continued under the Playhaven name. No longer seems active.

name: Branch
comment: SDK for Branch, a mobile linking and measurement platform: deferred deep linking, QR codes, campaign attribution.
Detail: Formerly named Branch Metrics, then renamed Branch (same company).

name: Microsoft Visual Studio App Center
comment: DevOps platform for building, testing, distributing and monitoring mobile apps; CodePush enabled live over-the-air updates to React/Cordova apps. Is no longer active as of 2025.
Detail: Owned by Microsoft. Evolved from HockeyApp (closed in 2019), but Microsoft closed this as well end of March 2025 and it is no longer active.

name: Adobe Experience Cloud
comment: Legacy Adobe Mobile SDK (ADBMobile) for analytics and marketing data collection. Discontinued.
Detail: Owned by Adobe Inc. Ended support in 2021, and was superseded with the newer Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) Mobile SDK.

name: Adobe Experience Cloud
comment: Current Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) Mobile SDK: modular SDK for analytics, identity and edge-network data collection, and has replaced the legacy ADBMobile SDK.
Detail: Owned by Adobe Inc.

name: MixPanel
comment: Product analytics platform: event tracking, funnels and user behavior analysis.
Detail: Owned by Mixpanel Inc.

name: Adjust
comment: Mobile attribution and marketing analytics platform: tracks ad campaign performance and app install attribution.
Detail: Owned by AppLovin Corporation. Formerly independent Adjust, acquired by AppLovin 2021, but remains its own brand and operates as a distinct product.

name: Amplitude
comment: Product analytics platform: event tracking, funnels, and user behavior analysis.
Detail: Owned by Amplitude, Inc. Incorporated as Sonalight, Inc. in 2011, renamed Amplitude Inc in 2014.

name: Heyzap (bought by Fyber)
comment: SDK for Heyzap, a mobile ad-mediation platform for game developers. Mediated interstitials, rewarded video, banners, and offerwalls across multiple ad networks.
Detail: Owned by Digital Turbine, Inc. Formerly independent Heyzap, acquired by Fyber in 2016, who was later on acquired by Digital Turbine in 2021. Discontinued as a standalone product.

name: Amazon Advertisement
comment: SDK for Amazon Mobile Ads, Amazon's own in-app advertising network. Served banner and interstitial ads using Amazon's shopping and browsing data for targeting. Discontinued in 2016.
Detail: Owned by Amazon.com, Inc. Discontinued and shutdown with service ending in 2016, so finding this regex signals an old codebase.

name: Vungle
comment: SDK for Vungle, a mobile video advertising platform. Delivers video ads and opt-in rewarded ads where users watch a video in exchange for in-app rewards.
Detail: Owned by Liftoff Mobile, Inc. (majority owned by Blackstone). Formerly independent Vungle merged with Liftoff in 2021. The brand Vungle itself is still active under Liftoff.

name: AppsFlyer
comment: SDK for AppsFlyer, a mobile measurement and attributition platform. Identifies which source - ad campaign, link or channel - led to each app install or in-app event. Handles deep links, which route users directly to specific screens in the app rather than the home screen. Also has tools to detect fraudulent installs.
Detail: Owned by AppsFlyer Ltd., got major investments in 2026 from Moloco, Google, Meta and Unity.

name: WeChat
comment: SDK for the WeChat Open Platform. Enables WeChat login, sharing and in-app payments in third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited. Formerly Weixin (2011), renamed to WeChat in 2012.

name: Baidu
comment: BMKMapView # Baidu Maps, BaiduMobStat # Baidu Analytics, BaiduMobAd # Baidu Ads. Catch-all signature covering multiple Baidu SDKs. E.g Maps, Analytics and Baidu Ads.
Detail: Owned by Baidu, Inc.

name: Umeng+
comment: SDK for Umeng, a mobile analytics, push-notification, and social-sharing platform. Tracks user behaviour, and crash data. handles push delivery across Chinese Android manufacturers (Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO, etc), which run their own push services instead of Google's. Legacy class name MobClick.
Detail: Owned by Alibaba Group. Formerly independent Umeng, acquired by Alibaba in 2013.

name: JiGuang Aurora Mobile JPush
comment: SDK for JPush (JiGuang), a push-notification service for mobile apps. Delivers push notifications to iOS devices and Android devices, including Chinese Android manufacturers (Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO, etc) that run their own push services instead of Google's.
Detail: Owned by Aurora Mobile Limited, founded in 2011. Originally branded 'Jiguang', rebranded 'Aurora Mobile' in 2015.

name: Tencent MTA
comment: SDK for Tencent Mobile Analytics (MTA), a mobile app analytics platform. Tracks user behaviour, session data, and retention for apps distributed in China. Status: possibly discontinued; little public activity since 2021. Effort from Tencent to move to its unified Tencent Cloud Mobile Analytics (MTA) platform
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited.

name: WeiboSDK
comment: SDK for Sina Weibo. Enables Weibo login and content-sharing inside third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by Weibo Corporation. Spun off from Sina Corporation in 2014; Sina Corporation retains 36% stake.

name: Bugly
comment: SDK for Tencent Bugly, a crash-reporting and beta-distribution platform. Captures crashes and exceptions and groups them by root cause. Supports over-the-air updates, where developers can push new builds to testers without going through the App store.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited. Closed-sourced.

name: Tencent Map LBS
comment: SDK for Tencent Maps. Embeds interactive maps, turn-by-turn routing, and location search into third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited.

name: WeChat Location
comment: SDK for Tencent Location Service (LBS). Retrieves a device's current location, converts addresses to coordinates (geocoding), and enables location-based features. Used across Tencent's apps, not exclusive to WeChat.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited

name: Alipay
comment: SDK for Alipay, a digital payments platform. Enables Alipay payments and checkout inside third-party apps. Widely used in apps targeting Chinese users.
Detail: Owned by Ant Group. Alipay spun off from Alibaba in 2011; reorganised as Ant Financial Services Group in 2014; renamed Ant Group in 2020). Alibaba holds a 1/3 stake.

name: Tencent Login
comment: SDK for Tencent OAuth login, that lets users sign in to third-party apps using their existing QQ or WeChat account.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited

name: ironSource
comment: SDK for ironSource (now LevelPlay), a mobile app monetization and mediation platform. Connects apps to multiple ad networks simultaneously and runs real-time auctions to select the highest-paying ad for each impression.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Formerly independent ironSource, merged into Unity in 2022. Fully rebranded as LevelPlay.

name: Startapp
comment: SDK for Start.io (Formerly StartApp), a mobile advertising and audience-data platform. Connects apps to multiple ad demand sources and delivers ads to users. Also collects app-usage signals to build audience segments for targeting.
Detail: Owned by Start.io, Inc. Founded 2010 as StartApp, rebranded to Start.io in 2021.

name: YouTube
comment: Library for embedding Youtube videos in iOS apps (youtube-ios-player-helper). It displayed YouTube's web-based player inside the app rather than providing a native video player. This project was archived by Google in 2024 and is no longer actively maintained.  Developers can instead now use the YouTube IFrame Player Api directly through WKWebView, or community wrappers around it.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet). Formerly independent YouTube, acquired by Google in 2006.

name: Google Tag Manager
comment: SDK for Google Tag Manager. Allows developers to update tracking, analytics, and marketing tags inside a live app without code changes or App store deployments.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: Pollfish
comment: SDK for Pollfish, a mobile market-research platform. Shows short surveys to app users during normal app use. App publishers receive payment for completed surveys; researchers receive consumer response data in real time.
Detail: Owned by Prodege LLC. Formerly independent Pollfish, acquired by Prodege in 2022.

name: Nexage
comment: SDK for Nexage (later Millennial Media), a mobile advertising exchange. Ran automated auctions where app publishers sold ad space to the highest-bidding advertiser in real time. Discontinued.
Detail: Last owned by Yahoo Inc. (Majority owned by Apollo Global Management). Formerly independent Nexage, acquired by Millennial Media in 2014; Millennial Media acquired by AOL in 2015; AOL became part of Verizon Media; Verizon Media sold to Apollo in 2021 and rebranded Yahoo Inc.

name: Flurry
comment: SDK for Flurry, a mobile app analytics and advertising platform. Tracked user sessions, retention and demographics. Also served ads via the Flurry Ads network. Discontinued in 2024.
Detail: Last owned by Yahoo Inc, who were bought by Apollo Global Management in 2021. Formerly independent Flurry, Inc., acquired by Yahoo in 2014. Became part of Verizon Media in 2017, and then sold 90% to Apollo, who then reverted it back to Yahoo Inc. in 2021.

name: Verizon Ads
comment: SDK for Verizon Ads, a mobile ad-serving platform built to replace the older Millennial Media and Flurry Ads SDKs. Delivered display, interstitial, and video ads to apps. Discontinued.
Detail: Last owned by Yahoo Inc. Built by Verizon Media as a successor to Millennial Media and Flurry Ads. Followed Yahoo's media business when Verizon sold it to Apollo Global Management in 2021.

name: Revmob
comment: SDK for RevMob, a mobile advertising network. Delivered interstitial and rewarded video ads to game-apps, paying publishers on a cost per mille (CPM)/cost per install (CPI) basis. Discontinued.
Detail: Owned by RevMob, the company seems to not be active anymore.

name: Amazon AWS
comment: Catch-all signature for Amazon Web Services (AWS) SDK classes embedded in an app. Covers integrations with AWS services such as storage, messaging, and compute. In documentation AWS recommend moving to AWS Amplify for Swift.
Detail: Owned by Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS division).

name: New Relic
comment: SDK for New Relic, an application performance monitoring and observability platform. Tracks app crashes, network request timing and errors, and user-interaction traces. Now an iOS Agent.
Detail: Owned by Francisco Partners and TPG. Formerly New Relic Inc, acquired by Francisco Partners and TPG in 2023.

name: Supersonic Ads
comment: SDK for Supersonic, a mobile ad-mediation platform for game apps. Ran video and rewarded ad campaigns across multiple ad networks.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Formerly an ironSource-owned brand, absorbed into ironSource in 2022, when Unity acquired ironSource.

name: Appodeal
comment: SDK for Appodeal, an automated mobile ad-monetisation platform. Connects apps to multiple ad demand sources at the same time and runs real-time auctions to select the highest-paying ad for each impression.
Detail: Owned by Appodeal, Inc.

name: Fyber
comment: SDK for Fyber (now rebranded as DT Exchange), a mobile advertising exchange and mediation platform. Connects apps to programmatic advertising buyers and runs real-time auctions for each ad impression. The SDK is now marketed as DT Exchange, and remains actively maintained.
Detail: Owned by Digital Turbine, Inc. Formerly independent SponsorPay, rebranded as Fyber in 2014; acquired Heyzap and Inneractive in 2016; was then acquired by Digital Turbine in 2021. Rebranded as DT Exchange after the acquisition.

name: Smaato
comment: SDK for Smaato, a mobile ad-exchange and ad-server platform - ran programmatic auctions for mobile inventory and provided tools for direct deals.
Detail: Owned by Verve Group. Formerly independent Smaato, acquired by Verve in 2021; the Smaato brand got folded into Verve's Brand+ Marketplace in 2024.

name: Urbanairship
comment: SDK for Airship (Formerly Urbanairship), a customer-engagement platform. Delivers push notifications, in-app messages, SMS, and email to app users.
Detail: Owned by Airship. Formerly Urban Airship, rebranded to Airship in 2019.

name: MobFox
comment: SDK for MobFox, a mobile advertising exchange and mediation platform. Connects app publishers to programmatic advertising buyers and runs auctions for ad inventory across banner, interstitial, video and native formats. Appears inactive.
Detail: Owned by Tightline holdings. Formerly independent MobFox, acquired by Matomy Media Group in 2014, then by Tightline Holdings in 2018.

name: Localytics
comment: SDK for Localytics, a mobile analytics and engagement platform. Tracks user behaviour and retention. Delivers push notification, in-app messages, and email campaigns based on the data it collects.
Detail: Owned by Upland Software, Inc. Formerly independent Localytics, acquired by Upland in 2020.

name: Appcelerator Analytics
comment: SDK for Appcelerator Analytics, the analytics module for applications built with the Appcelerator Titanium framework. Tracks application usage and events through the Appcelerator Platform. Status: discontinued in 2022.
Detail: Developed by Appcelerator, acquired by Axway in 2016. Axway discontinued the Appcelerator platform, and the analytics service is now no longer maintained. The Titanium SDK lives on through the community-maintained TiDev, but this service is not a part of it.

name: AdBuddiz
comment: SDK for AdBuddiz, a mobile interstitial ad network. Serves full-screen static and video ads to game and app publishers.
Detail: Owned by AdBuddiz. Appears inactive.

name: Radius Networks
comment: SDK for ProximityKit, a beacon and indoor-location platform. Detects nearby Bluetooth beacons to trigger location-aware experiences in apps, such as retail notifications or venue check-ins. Status: iOS repos has had no public activity in a long time, might be discontinued.
Detail: Owned by Radius Networks, Inc.

name: AdTech Mobile SDK
comment: SDK for ADTECH, a legacy mobile ad-serving platform. Delivered targeted display, and rich-media ads to mobile ads. Status: discontinued.
Detail: Last owned by Yahoo Inc., (Owned by Apollo Global Management). AdTech was acquired by AOL in 2007; AOL became part of Verizon Media in 2015; Verizon Media was acquired by Apollo Global Management in 2021, and rebranded as Yahoo Inc.

name: ComScore
comment: SDK for ComScore/ComScoreAnalytics, an audience-measurement platform. Measures app reach, unique visitors, demographics, and content engagement. Data is used by publishers and advertisers for planning and campaign verification.
Detail: Owned by Comscore, Inc.

name: Soomla
comment: SDK for Soomla, an open-source mobile game development framework. Provided virtual economy tools - in-app store scaffolding, currency systems, and item management for game developers. Status: no longer actively maintained.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Formerly independent Soomla, acquired by ironSource in 2021, who later merged into Unity in 2022.

name: BugSense
comment: SDK for BugSense, a mobile crash-reporting and analytics platform. Automatically captured crashes and exceptions, grouped them by stack trace, and surfaced them in a developer dashboard. Status: discontinued.
Detail: Last owned by Cisco Systems. Formerly independent BugSense, acquired by Splunk in 2013, and renamed Splunk MINT Express; Splunk was acquired by Cisco in 2024. Discontinued.
link: https://grokipedia.com/page/bugsense (third-party reference page, but no official documentation is found)

name: Yandex Ad
comment: SDK for Yandex Ads, a mobile advertising platform. Serves display, video, and native ads to app developers. Primarily used for apps distributed in Russia and CIS markets.
Detail: Owned by IPJSC Yandex, controlled by Consortium.First ( a group of Russian investors and senior Yandex managers). In 2024 Dutch parent Yandex N.V sold its Russian businesses to Consortium.First; Yandex N.V. renamed its remaining international activities Nebius Group. Yandex Ads stayed with the Russian domestic entity. Consortium.First is managed by Solid Management.
Website: https://ads.yandex.com, https://cbonds.com/etf/210495/, https://yandex.com/company/news/05-02-2024, https://solid-mn.ru/ (last one might be difficult to open but should be the management website)

name: AppMetrica
comment: SDK for AppMetrica, a mobile analytics, attribution and crash-reporting platform. Tracks user behaviour, installs, and campaign attribution. Mainly used by apps distributed in Russia and CIS markets.
Detail: Owned by Yandex LLC, controlled by Consortium.First ( a group of Russian investors and senior Yandex managers). In 2024 Dutch parent Yandex N.V sold its Russian businesses to Consortium.First; Yandex N.V. renamed its remaining international activities Nebius Group. Yandex Ads stayed with the Russian domestic entity. Consortium.First is managed by Solid Management.

name: Mail.ru
comment: SDK for Mail.ru (now VK). Provides login and social features for third-party apps. Also bundles myTarget advertising capabilities.
Detail: Owned by VK Company Limited, majority controlled by Sogaz Insurance Group and Gazprom Media Holding. Formerly Mail.ru Group, renamed VK in 2021.

name: Quantcast
comment: SDK for Quantcast, an audience measurement and advertising platform. Measures app reach, unique visitors, and demographics. Seems discontinued
Detail: Owned by Quantcast Corporation. Note: Quantcast sold its Choice consent-management product to InMobi in 2023; this entry tracks the separate audience-measurement SDK.

name: VKontakte SDK
comment: SDK for VKontakte (VK). Enables VK login and sharing inside third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by VK Company Limited, majority controlled by Sogaz Insurance Group and Gazprom Media Holding. Formerly Mail.ru Group, renamed VK in 2021

name: Batch
comment: SDK for Batch, a mobile marketing-automation platform. Handles push notifications, in-app messages, and automated user journeys.
Detail: Owned by Batch SAS.

name: Tapdaq
comment: SDK for Tapdaq, a mobile ad-mediation platform for game developers. Mediated demand from multiple ad networks for interstitial and rewarded ad formats. Status: discontinued as a standalone product, absorbed into Tapjoy in 2018, and then into Unity via ironSource.
Detail: Owned by Unity Software Inc. Formerly independent Tapdaq, acquired by Tapjoy in 2018, who was then acquired by ironSource in 2021; ironSource merged into Unity in 2022.

name: Sentry
comment: SDK for Sentry, an error-tracking and application-monitoring platform. Automatically captures unhandled exceptions and crashes in real time, groups them by root cause, and provides stack traces and session data to help developers reproduce and fix issues.
Detail: Owned by Sentry (legal name Functional Software Inc).

name: Kakao
comment: SDK for Kakao. Enables KakaoTalk login and sharing inside third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by Kakao Corp. Formed via the 2014 merger of Kakao Inc. with Daum Communications (very briefly called Daum Kakao, reverted back to Kakao in 2015). Daum was spun back off as an independent subsidiary in 2025.

name: Fyber SponsorPay
comment: SDK for SponsorPay - the legacy version of what later became Fyber. Provided rewarded ad placements and offerwalls, where users complete an action in exchange for in-app rewards. Status: discontinued.
Detail: Owned by Digital Turbine, Inc. Formerly independent SponsorPay, rebranded as Fyber in 2014; acquired Heyzap and Inneractive in 2016; was then acquired by Digital Turbine in 2021. Rebranded as DT Exchange after the acquisition.

name: Ooyala
comment: SDK for Ooyala, a cloud video platform. Provided a video player, transcoding, content management, and analytics for media companies. Status: discontinued in 2020.
Detail: Owned by Brightcove Inc. Formerly majority owned by Telstra (2012-2019), the video platform busines was acquired by Brightcove in 2019.

name: Google Firebase Analytics
comment: SDK for Firebase Analytics, Google's mobile app analytics service. Tracks user behaviour, in-app events, and audience segmentations. Also surfaces as Google App Measurement, alternative class names include (APMAnalytics|APMMeasurement)
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet). Part of the Firebase SDK Suite.

name: iAd
comment: Apple's own mobile advertising platform, used to serve ads to third-party apps via an Apple-managed network. Status: discontinued in 2016. AdClient and AAAtribution are the legacy class names; Apple's current attribution tool is SKAdNetwork.
Detail: Owned by Apple Inc.

name: Apple SKAdNetwork
comment: Attribution framework. Used by ad networks to measure which ads led to app installs, without access to individual device identifiers or personal data. Built into iOS, and is not a third-party SDK.
Detail: Owned by Apple Inc.

name: CleverTap
comment: SDK for CleverTap, a customer-engagement and product analytics platform. Tracks user behaviour and retention. Runs push-notifications, in-apps messages, and A/B tests based on that data.
Detail: Owned by CleverTap, Inc.

name: Sensors Analytics
comment: SDK for Sensors Analytics (神策数据),  a product-analytics platform. Tracks user behaviour, event funnels, and retention. Used a lot by apps distributed in China.
Detail: Owned by Sensors Data (Shence Network Technology Co., Ltd., 神策网络科技).

name: Braze (formerly Appboy)
comment: SDK for Braze (formerly Appboy), a customer-engagement platform. Handles push notifications, in app messages, email, and SMS campaigns.
Detail: Owned by Braze. Formerly Appboy, renamed Braze in 2017.

name: Bugsnag
comment: SDK for Bugsnag, an error-monitoring platform. Captures and automatically groups crashes and exceptions by root cause. Shows how many users and sessions are affected by each issue.
Detail: Owned by SmartBear Software. Formerly independent Bugsnag, acquired by SmartBear in 2021.

name: myTarget
comment: SDK for myTarget, a programmatic advertising platform. Serves display, video, and native ads across VK's social network, Odnoklassniki, and partner apps.
Detail: Owned by VK Company Limited. Formerly Mail.ru Group, renamed VK in 2021.

name: Tencent Ads
comment: SDK for Tencent Ads (Guangdiantong/GDT), Tencent's mobile advertising platform. Serves targeted display, video, and native ads across WeChat, QQ, and Tencent's partner network.
Detail: Owned by Tencent Holdings Limited.

name: Kochava
comment: SDK for Kochava, a mobile measurement platform. Identifies which marketing channel drove each app install or in-app event, tracks fraud and provides ROI analytics for campaigns.
Detail: Owned by Kochava Inc.

name: Mintegral
comment: SDK for Mintegral, a programmatic mobile advertising platform. Serves interactive and video ads, and connect app publishers to global ad demand through in-app bidding.
Detail: Owned by Mobvista Inc.

name: Pangle
comment: SDK for Pangle, a mobile advertising network. Serves video and interactive ads to apps outside of TikTok/Douyin. Bytedance Ads.
Detail: Owned by Bytedance Ltd.

name: AdColony
comment: SDK for AdColony, a mobile advertising network for video and rich media ads: shows video and interactive rich-media ads to support monetization
Detail: Owned by Affle. Formerly owned by Digital Turbine who acquired it in 2021 from Otello Corp. Digital Turbine discontinued the SDK and sold the AdColony brand, SDK and the underlying technology to Affle (Affle MEA FZ LLC) in 2026.

name: Firestore
comment: SDK for Google Firestore, a NoSQL cloud-database service. Stores structured app data, syncs it in real time across all connected clients, and supports offline access with automatic conflict resolution. Part of the Firebase and Google Cloud platform families.
Detail: Owned by Google LLC (Alphabet).

name: HelpShift
comment: SDK for HelpShift, a customer-support platform. Provides an in-app help desk with chat, FAQs, and ticket management, so users can get support without leaving the app.
Detail: Owned by Keywords Studios (acquired by EQT in 2024). Formerly independent HelpShift, acquired by Keywords Studios in 2022.

name: Emarsys
comment: SDK for Emarsys, a marketing-automation and customer-engagement platform. Handles push notifications, in-app messages, and email campaigns with personalisation and segmentation tools.
Detail: Owned by SAP SE. Formerly independent Emarsys, acquired by SAP in 2020.

name: RevenueCat
comment: SDK for RevenueCat, a subscription-management platform. Handles in-app purchase logic, manages entitlements across platforms, and provides analytics on subscription revenue, churn, and trials.
Detail: Owned by RevenueCat, Inc.

name: Bugfender
comment: SDK for Bugfender, a remote log-management service. Collects and stores mobile app logs in the cloud so developers can inspect them without needing to reproduce issues locally.
Detail: Owned by Bugfender, a spin off from the parent company Mobile Jazz.

name: NStack
comment: SDK for NStack, a backend-as-a-service platform. Provides version control for app copy and strings, GEO information, APP Store rate reminders, and other app-utility services.
Detail: Owned by Monstarlab.

name: Mapbox
comment: SDK for Mapbox, a mapping and location platform. Provides customisable map tiles, routing, navigation, and geospatial search that can be embedded in apps
Detail: Owned by Mapbox, Inc.

name: Exponea
comment: SDK for Exponea, a customer-data and experience platform. Unifies customer data, tracks behaviour and retention, and runs personalised ad campaigns.
Detail: Owned by Bloomreach. Formerly independent Exponea, acquired by Bloomreach in 2021.

name: OneSignal
comment: SDK for OneSignal, a email, sms, push notification, and in-app message service for mobile apps. Includes real-time updates, reminders, and personalized messages
Detail: Owned by OneSignal Inc.

name: Forter
comment: SDK for Forter, a 'fraud prevention analytics'. This includes behavioral analysis of customers' established shopping patterns, soft linking. Automatic analysis of transactions and users
Detail: Owned by Forter Inc.

name: Alibaba Cloud
comment: Catch-all signature for Alibaba Cloud, also known as Aliyun, SDK components. Libraries for connecting apps to Alibaba's cloud-computing services including storage, compute, CDN, and security.
Detail: Owned by Alibaba Group. Aliyun/Alibaba Cloud is a subsidiary of Alibaba Group.

name: Alipay SDK
comment: Alipay SDK is a payment SDK. Enables Alipay payments and checkout inside third-party apps.
Detail: Owned by Ant Group. Alipay spun off from Alibaba in 2011; reorganised as Ant Financial Services Group in 2014; renamed Ant Group in 2020). Alibaba holds a 1/3 stake.

name: Baidu Mobile Stat
comment: SDK for Baidu Mobile Stat, Baidu's mobile app analytics service. Tracks user sessions, behaviour, and retention for apps distributed in China.
Detail: Owned by Baidu, Inc.

name: Baidu Mobile Ads
comment: SDK for Baidu Mobile Ads, Baidu's mobile advertising service. Serves ads from Baidu's advertiser network to apps distributed in China.
Detail: Owned by Baidu, Inc.

name: Alibaba Map service
comment: SDK for AMap (Gaode Maps), a mapping and location-services platform. Provides map tiles, routing, Points of Interest search, and location APIs for apps distributed in China.
Detail: Owned by Alibaba Group. Formerly independent Autonavi (branded AMap for consumers), fully acquired by Alibaba in 2014.

name: Imgix
comment: SDK for Imgix, a real-time image processing service. Transforms, optimises, and delivers images via CDN on request.
Detail: Owned by Imgix, Inc.

name: Mindbox
comment: SDK for Mindbox, a marketing automation platform. This SDK allows developers to integrate mobile push notifications, in-app messages, and client events into iOS projects.
Detail: Owned by Mindbox, russian marketing automation platform. Founded 2006, backed by Baring Vostok (minority investor, 2022)

name: Amazon Chime SDK
comment: SDK for Amazon Chime. A set of real-time communications components that developers can use to quickly add audio, video, and screen sharing capabilities to their own applications.
Detail: Owned by Amazon.com (AWS division).

name: OneTrust
comment: SDK for OneTrust, a privacy management platform. Collects and manages user consent for GDPR, CCPA, and other privacy regulations, and handles data-subject requests.
Detail: Owned by OneTrust LLC.

name: BidMachine
comment: SDK for BidMachine, an in-app bidding platform operated by Appodeal. Runs server-side auctions across multiple ad buyers for each ad impression, replacing tradition fixed-priority ad-waterfall with a real-time auction.
Detail: Owned by Appodeal, Inc.

name: Amazon SNS
comment: SDK for Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS), a managed pub/sub messaging service. Routes messages between app components and microservices, and can deliver push notifications to mobile devices.
Detail: Owned by Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS division).

name: Usabilla
comment: SDK for Usabilla. The SDK allows for collecting in-app user feedback through surveys, campaigns, feedback forms, and screenshot-based bug reports.
Detail: Originally developed by Usabilla. Acquired by SurveyMonkey in 2019, which rebranded as Momentive in 2021. Momentive was acquired by Symphony Technology Group in 2023, who reverted to the SurveyMonkey brand. The SDK is available under SurveyMonkey branding.

name: MobileFuse
comment: SDK for MobileFuse, a mobile advertising platform. Serves contextual and location-based ads to app publishers.
Detail: Owned by MobileFuse.

name: Smaato
comment: SDK for Smaato, a mobile ad-exchange and ad-server platform - ran programmatic auctions for mobile inventory and provided tools for direct deals.
Detail: Owned by Verve Group. Formerly independent Smaato, acquired by Verve in 2021; the Smaato brand got folded into Verve's Brand+ Marketplace in 2024.

name: Apptentive
comment: SDK for Apptentive, a customer-feedback platform. Triggers targeted in-app surveys, rating prompts, and feedback forms based on user behaviour and sentiment signals.
Detail: Owned by Alchemer. Formerly independent Apptentive, acquired by Alchemer in 2023. Alchemer itself is backed by private equity firm KKR.

name: Braintree
comment: SDK for Braintree, a payment platform. Handles card payments, PayPal, Venmo, and other payment methods inside apps, including tokenisation, vaulting, and 3D secure authentication.
Detail: Owned by PayPal Holdings, Inc. Formerly independent Braintree, acquired by PayPal in 2013.

name: umeng
comment: SDK for Umeng's mobile app analytics. Tracks user behaviour, retention, and device data.
Detail: Owned by Alibaba Group. Formerly independent Umeng, acquired by Alibaba in 2013.
